content.user_title: Manage Azure Key Vault Keys in Java
content.value_statement: Java teams need secure examples for Azure Key Vault key operations. This skill gives focused Java SDK guidance for key clients, cryptographic operations, rotation, and recovery.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for azure-security-keyvault-keys 4.9.0.
Demonstrates KeyClient and CryptographyClient creation with DefaultAzureCredential.
Explains RSA, EC, OCT, and HSM-backed key options.
Covers encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify, wrap, and unwrap operations.
Includes key backup, restore, rotation policy, import, and error handling examples.
limitations: Requires an existing Azure tenant, vault, permissions, and valid credentials.
Examples use placeholders and must be adapted before production use.
Does not design full key governance, RBAC, or compliance controls.
Does not replace security review of algorithms, key lifetimes, or data flows.

use_cases.title: Configure Java Key Clients
use_cases.description: Set up Java services to use Azure Key Vault keys with managed identity and vault URLs.

use_cases.title: Review Cryptographic Workflows
use_cases.description: Check key types, allowed operations, and rotation policies before implementation.

use_cases.title: Add Application Crypto Operations
use_cases.description: Plan encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify, wrap, and unwrap flows for Java services.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Key Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to set up an Azure Key Vault Keys client in Java using DefaultAzureCredential and a vault URL placeholder.

prompt_templates.title: Create Production Keys
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose RSA, EC, or HSM-backed keys for a Java service. Include key operations and expiration guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Add Crypto Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Java workflow for encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify, wrap, and unwrap using Azure Key Vault Keys.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Rotation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned key rotation and backup process for Azure Key Vault. Identify security gaps, missing permissions, and operational risks.

output_examples.input: I need to create an HSM-backed RSA key for a payment service.
output_examples.output: Recommended key type, size, operations, expiration, and Java SDK steps for an HSM-backed RSA key.

output_examples.input: I need to verify signatures from a Java service.
output_examples.output: A concise workflow covering digest creation, signing, verification, and algorithm selection with Azure Key Vault.

output_examples.input: I need a key rotation plan.
output_examples.output: Rotation timing, policy actions, rollback notes, and checks for soft delete, permissions, and monitoring.

best_practices: Use HSM-backed keys for production secrets and regulated workloads.
Assign only the key operations each application actually needs.
Test rotation, recovery, and deletion flows in a nonproduction vault first.
anti_patterns: Hard-coding real vault names, key identifiers, credentials, or private key material in prompts.
Using broad Key Vault permissions when a service only needs one operation.
Copying sample algorithms without checking application threat models and compliance needs.

faq.question: Does this skill manage secrets?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Key Vault keys and cryptographic operations, not secrets or certificates.

faq.question: Which Java SDK is covered?
faq.answer: It covers the Azure Security Key Vault Keys Java SDK and related cryptography client classes.

faq.question: Can it create HSM-backed keys?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include RSA and EC keys with hardware protection options.

faq.question: Does it run Azure commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and Java examples. Users run adapted code in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it review existing Java code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the relevant code and goals, then ask for key management or cryptography guidance.

faq.question: Is expert security review still needed?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it as implementation guidance, not final approval for cryptographic design or compliance.
